correctness.rationale: The decomposition P_e=product of commuting E_i and I-E_i gives orthogonal free direct summands and a bijection with bit-pattern-labeled direct-sum decompositions; GL_n(R) acts transitively with product stabilizers. Signed-Stirling inversion precisely counts distinct commuting tuples. Maximal cliques are Boolean projection systems whose atoms must have free rank one, and any primitive frame is maximal. All boundaries n>=1, k>=0, zero/identity vertices and coefficients are explicit. Direct exhaustive ring arithmetic and graph enumeration in six small finite local examples returned VERIFY_OK; finite tests corroborate rather than prove the unrestricted theorem.

value.rationale: Every clique number and every maximal commuting family of idempotents is a natural global invariant of a nontrivial graph family. Its complete computation for all n and all finite commutative local rings yields a structural universality result across inequivalent rings with equal size and residue order (for instance Z/4Z and F_2[epsilon]/epsilon^2). It is not a renaming of the known one-idempotent census or k=2 field case; it determines the entire compatible-projection complex, its maximal face count, and vertex links.
